title: Indirect Prompt Injection in Browser-Using Agents: A Systematic Analysis from MCP to Host Compromise
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: indirect prompt injection; LLM agents; Model Context Protocol; web security; threat model; adversarial robustness; prompt injection defense
topics: Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning; Web Application Security Vulnerabilities; Security and Verification in Computing
abstract: Browser-Using Agents (BUAs) are an emerging class of LLM-powered agents that interact with web browsers autonomously, navigating pages, filling forms, and executing multi-step tasks on behalf of users. Because these agents consume untrusted web content and incorporate it into their reasoning context, they are inherently exposed to indirect prompt injection (IPI)—attacks in which adversarial instructions embedded in external data sources are interpreted by the model as authoritative commands. This work provides a systematic analysis of IPI severity in BUAs by tracing the threat from its protocol-level enablers to concrete browser-level exploitation. I formalize the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the technical substrate through which IPI payloads reach the agent, analyze the browser control stack (CDP, Chromium isolation, automation frameworks) to show that no downstream layer offers principled containment against semantic-level compromise, and demonstrate that conventional web security mechanisms provide at best incidental defense. I further systematize MCP-native threats as upstream IPI vectors, survey state-of-the-art defense and attack techniques, and present a formal threat model grounding an end-to-end robustness benchmark of BUAs under realistic adversarial constraints.

title: LOCI AI v1.a: Unified Architecture for Personal, Verifiable, and Federable AI Memory (RAG + TOON + KG + CRDT + ZK + SBT)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

topics: Blockchain Technology Applications and Security; Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Topic Modeling
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are inherently stateless, lacking persistent memory between sessions. Centralized persistence models compromise user privacy, cognitive sovereignty, and intellectual property. We propose LOCI AI v1.a, a unified architecture comprising three operational phases: Phase 1 (On-Device): Personal memory stored locally with dual-format JSON-LD/TOON representation; Phase 1.5 (Hybrid): Architecture with a Sovereignty Guardian that manages local/cloud exchanges with data obfuscation and cryptographic notarization; Phase 2 (Federated): P2P federation with CRDT-based synchronization, ZK-Proof verification, and Soulbound Tokens for intellectual property anchoring. The Operational Standard v1.4.3 defines an executable protocol and validation constraints. Empirical validation demonstrates 41.2% token efficiency improvement (TOON) and RAG Recall@3 of 0.94. This paper unifies theoretical vision, pragmatic implementation, and technical roadmap with emphasis on energy efficiency and GDPR compliance. title: AI-NATIVE DLP: REPLACING REGEX-BASED CONTENT INSPECTION WITH LLM-DRIVEN SEMANTIC UNDERSTANDING FOR ENTERPRISE DATA EXFILTRATION DETECTION
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: data loss prevention; data exfiltration detection; false positive reduction; insider threat detection; enterprise data security
topics: Information and Cyber Security; Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning
abstract: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) has been a cornerstone of enterprise security for over two decades, yet its foundationaltechnology-regular expression (regex) pattern matching, keyword blocklists, and exact-match fingerprinting-wasdesigned for an era of structured, predictable data flows. The explosion of unstructured data, GenAI-poweredworkflows, and shadow AI adoption has exposed the fundamental limitations of pattern-based DLP: industry datashows that legacy DLP systems achieve 5–25% accuracy on unstructured content classification, generate false positiverates exceeding 40% on complex data types, and provide zero visibility into GenAI prompt-based data exfiltrationchannels. This paper introduces the paradigm of AI-Native DLP-a fundamental architectural shift from regex-basedcontent inspection to LLM-driven semantic understanding for enterprise data exfiltration detection. We present acomprehensive analysis comparing three generations of DLP technology across seven data categories and sevenexfiltration channels, demonstrating that LLM-driven semantic inspection achieves 82–98% detection accuracy acrossall content types (compared to 8–96% for regex), reduces false positive rates from 37–42% to 3.5–5% over twelvemonths of production deployment, and extends coverage to previously undetectable channels including GenAIprompts, browser-based paste operations, and paraphrased confidential data. We evaluate the architectural patterns,latency characteristics, cost implications, enterprise deployment challenges, regulatory compliance alignment, insiderthreat detection capabilities, LLM model selection trade-offs, and shadow AI governance of AI-native DLP, andpresent a maturity model for organizations transitioning from legacy to semantic-first data protection. Our analysisdraws on published performance data from Nightfall AI, Lakera, Cyera, Concentric AI, Cloudflare AI Gateway, andMicrosoft Purview, alongside academic research on LLM-based content classification and the OWASP frameworkfor LLM application security

title: An agentic LLM-powered recommendation system using tools, templates and prompt engineering
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: recommender systems; cold start; personalization; large language models; semantic search; prompt engineering; cross-domain recommendation; explainable recommendation; content-based filtering; e-commerce recommendation; movie recommendation; user constraints; embedding models
topics: Recommender Systems and Techniques; Information Retrieval and Search Behavior; Advanced Bandit Algorithms Research
abstract: Cold start and personalization remain fundamental challenges in recommender systems, particularly in e-commerce and entertainment platforms where new users and items lack historical interaction. Our paper proposes a cross-domain, Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered recommendation framework that mitigates cold start by shifting from interaction-based learning to semantic understanding and reasoning over heterogeneous textual and contextual information. The system integrates three embedding models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2, multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1) for semantic retrieval with two open-source LLMs to generate adaptive, explainable recommendations through natural language interaction. An agentic filtering mechanism dynamically incorporates user constraints such as category, usage scenario, price range and ratings, while prompt templates include user attributes and prior purchases to enhance personalization. The approach combines semantic similarity, reasoning-driven recommendation powered by a local model llama3.1:8b or Groq-hosted llama-3.3-70b-versatile model and content-based signals within a unified architecture. The embedding models are evaluated using ranking and retrieval metrics (Precision@K, Recall@K, NDCG@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank, Hit Rate@K, catalog coverage). Experimental validation is conducted across two distinct domains: retail products and movies, using publicly available datasets from Hugging Face and Kaggle platforms. The proposed framework is dataset-agnostic, explainable by design and readily transferable across domains, offering a scalable solution for cold start-aware recommendation systems.

abstract: Retail investors face significant challenges in processinglarge volumes of unstructured financial data from multipledisparate sources, leading to information asymmetry andpoor investment decisions. This paper presents Vest.ai, a multiagentinvestment research assistant that orchestrates specializedagents for data collection, sentiment analysis, financial metricscomputation, and report generation. The novelty of this worklies in its hybrid ensemble architecture integrating a lightweightNode.js orchestrator with a specialized Python-based sentimentengine, explicitly designed to democratize institutional-gradeanalysis for retail investors. By integrating Google GeminiLLM, Python-based NLP models, and real-time financial APIsthrough a unified Node.js backend, Vest.ai employs Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground LLM outputs in realmarket data, significantly improving reliability and mitigatinghallucination. Comprehensive validation demonstrates 98.66%sentiment accuracy via an ensemble meta-learner and 5-secondaverage report generation time. This work addresses criticalgaps in explainability, real-time integration, and customization,presenting a production-ready prototype for scalable multi-agentfinancial systems.

title: A Survey of Natural-Language Driven Command-Line Assistants and Intelligent Shell Systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Prof. Nikhil Agrawal; Anushka Patil; Nikhil Kurkure; Dheesh Medekar; Renesh Sharma; Kuntal Thakur
keywords: large language models; hallucinations; error handling; transformer models
topics: Software Engineering Research; Natural Language Processing Techniques; Speech and dialogue systems
abstract: - For decades, the command-line interface has been fundamental to system administration, software development, and automation, supporting both professionals and advanced users.Its usability however has been restricted and intimidating to say the very least as a user is required to memorize the commands and syntax. With recent breakthroughs in NLP and LLM based architectures in quite literally everything the traditional CLIs are being integrated with them these as well. This survey brings together the latest research and practical system developments in natural language powered command line assistants and automated shell systems. We start by looking at how CLIs have evolved historically and examining early automation technologies, tracing the journey from manually crafted scripts to neural network approaches that harness the capabilities of modern transformer models. The paper presents a systematic way to classify intelligent shell systems based on their underlying model architecture, how they decide whether to execute commands, their safety measures, and their strategies for handling errors. We evaluate several representative systems including ShellGPT, Warp AI, Copilot CLI, and our own hybrid assistant that combines both local and cloud-based language models using detailed comparison matrices and real world use case analysis. We dive deep into the major challenges these systems face: hallucinations where the AI generates incorrect commands, ambiguous error messages that are hard to interpret, limited training data, and serious security concerns. Finally, we explore where future research should head, imagining the next wave of autonomous system administration agents, secure on-device AI inference, and voice controlled CLI automation. This survey contributes a unified classification system, an extensive literature review, empirically grounded comparisons between systems, and practical recommendations for researchers and developers who want to build robust, intelligent command line automation tools, to say the very least the final target is to help create something at the kernel level which will be an assisted mechanism for the entire os and all applications within it.

title: Mobile Background Processing for Persistent On-Device Cognitive AI Systems: A Technical Survey
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Mohamed Reezan Mohd Fadzil; Kah Mun Chan
keywords: Core ML; MLX; llama.cpp; preemption
topics: Mobile and Web Applications; Green IT and Sustainability; Parallel Computing and Optimization Techniques
abstract: Overview This paper presents a comprehensive technical survey of mobile background processing frameworks and on-device AI inference capabilities, conducted from the perspective of a practitioner who has designed and deployed a production persistent cognitive AI system on iOS. No proprietary system design, unpublished technical implementation, or pending intellectual property is disclosed. All material surveyed is drawn from publicly available platform documentation, developer resources, and open-access research. The Engineering Problem Persistent, always-on cognitive AI systems — on-device AI that maintains continuous user context and identity state across sessions separated by hours or days — require periodic background maintenance operations that cannot be completed during active user sessions alone. Mobile operating systems impose strict constraints on background execution. This survey characterises what is actually possible within those constraints in 2026, rather than what is conventionally assumed. Scope Three interrelated bodies of publicly documented technical material are surveyed in depth: (1) the iOS background task execution framework, covering BGAppRefreshTask, BGProcessingTask, and the BGContinuedProcessingTask introduced in iOS 26, including scheduling heuristics, constraint configuration, preemption handling, and the BackgroundTasks framework evolution from iOS 7 through iOS 26; (2) the Android background processing framework, covering WorkManager, JobScheduler, Doze mode, and App Standby bucket policies, including the historical evolution from AlarmManager and legacy background services to the modern declarative constraint model; and (3) the on-device AI inference landscape under mobile hardware constraints, including battery and thermal characterisation across CPU, GPU, and Apple Neural Engine (ANE) execution pathways, quantisation strategies for memory-feasible on-device model deployment, thermal throttling behaviour under sustained inference load, and the current mobile LLM inference framework landscape including Core ML, MLX, llama.cpp, MLC-LLM, and ANEMLL. Key Findings Mobile platforms in 2026 provide a richer and more capable background execution environment for AI workloads than is commonly assumed. BGProcessingTask with charging-state constraints and the newly introduced BGContinuedProcessingTask together enable meaningful AI maintenance workloads during device idle periods on iOS. Android's WorkManager provides equivalent capability with guaranteed task persistence across device reboots. Both platforms converge on the overnight charging period as the optimal execution window for compute-intensive AI maintenance. At 4-bit quantisation, 1B–3B parameter models are memory-feasible on current iPhone hardware and can execute at 9–62 tokens per second via the Apple Neural Engine at approximately 2 watts — a power budget compatible with charging-period background execution. Design Implications The survey derives a comprehensive set of design principles for persistent cognitive AI systems on mobile: treating background execution windows as first-class architectural primitives; implementing checkpoint-resume patterns for preemption safety; selecting low-power inference pathways for battery conservation; and scheduling maintenance operations around charging-constrained windows rather than deferring them opportunistically. Structure 10 sections · 9 figures · 35 references · ~11,000 words · Compliant with ISO 214, ISO 215, ISO 690, and APA 7th Edition citation standards. title: rmt-llm-research — Random Matrix Theory meets Large Language Models: spectral analysis of activations and the mathematical inevitability of hallucinations
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: random matrix theory; large language models; hallucinations; covariance matrix; Marchenko-Pastur distribution; Tracy-Widom distribution; reinforcement learning from human feedback; Fokker-Planck equation; winding number
topics: Random Matrices and Applications; Topic Modeling; Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning
abstract: A research repository by Iskhak Hamzatovich Isaev presenting a comprehensive program applying Random Matrix Theory (RMT) to the analysis of large language models (LLMs). Thread 1 — Spectral statistics of LLM activations. Covariance matrices of GPT-2 hidden-state activations exhibit fundamentally different spectral properties in factual recall vs creative generation mode. The BBP phase transition, Marchenko-Pastur bounds, and Tracy-Widom fluctuations provide quantitative markers for cognitive mode detection. Thread 2 — Mathematical proof of inevitable hallucinations. Ten independent mathematical paths converge on a single critical token count N_crit: complex phase, operator dynamics, GUE spectral statistics, thermodynamic entropy, Lévy-Langevin fractional dynamics, EP-surfaces, Tracy-Widom, quantum channel degradation, NHSE (winding number), and Caputo fractional-time memory. Thread 3 — The utility trap: RLHF and entropic collapse. RLHF optimization creates an artificial drift in the Fokker-Planck equation, forcing the model to «lie beautifully once» rather than risk a self-correction cycle. With Caputo memory parameter β ≈ 0.5, the mean collapse time scales as ⟨T_crit⟩ ∝ (μ_eff)-2 — even small RLHF pressure quadratically accelerates hallucination onset. The repository ships 12 DOCX monographs (EN/RU), 1 PDF paper, a GitHub Pages documentation site, an interactive in-browser demo, a Python verification package (rmt_llm) with 70+ pytest tests, a Julia verification package (RMTLLMVerify), and a Jupyter verification notebook.

title: Towards AI-Driven Adaptive Reading: Gaze-Aware Support in Digital Environments
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Manuel Munoz Martinez; Matteo Lisi; Jessie Ricketts; Alireza Tamaddoni‐Nezhad
keywords: eye tracking; digital reading; large language models; sentence simplification; real-time intervention; information overload; attention fragmentation; inclusive design; inductive logic programming; few-shot learning; usability evaluation
topics: Gaze Tracking and Assistive Technology; Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning; Digital Accessibility for Disabilities
abstract: Can digital reading be made more responsive to individual cognitive needs? This work introduces an adaptive reading system that leverages eye-tracking and AI to provide real-time support aimed at reducing distraction and improving the overall reading experience. Digital reading environments often impose cognitive constraints, including information overload and attentional fragmentation. To address these challenges, the proposed system enables the detection of reading difficulties as they occur. We present a working prototype that integrates a Python interface with a Tobii Nano Pro eye tracker (60 Hz), a WebSocket server for real-time communication, and a Chrome extension for in-browser interaction. When predefined criteria are met, such as prolonged fixations (>800 ms) or repeated scanning patterns, a local large language model (via Ollama) generates context-aware interventions, including definitions, translations and sentence simplification. We conducted an empirical evaluation (n=20) assessing usability and acceptance through comprehension questions, qualitative feedback, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). This initial evaluation aims to establish a baseline for future development of an adaptive layer, built using inductive logic programming (ILP), that can adapt to individual reading behaviours through few-shot interaction. Particular emphasis is placed on inclusive design, with the aim of supporting readers with diverse needs.Poster presented at ECEM 2026, Ulm (Germany), 30 Aug - 4 Sep 2026.

title: RoboSafe: A Quantitative Character Safety Certification Framework for Social Robot Deployments in Public-Facing Environments
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: social robots; key performance indicators; drift monitoring; compliance monitoring; AI governance
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI; Social Robot Interaction and HRI; Safety Systems Engineering in Autonomy
abstract: We present the RoboSafe Standard v1.0, a normative certification framework for the charac- ter safety layer of physical AI systems — robots and AI-driven hardware that interact with hu- man beings in physical spaces. As large language models are increasingly deployed on embodied platforms (wheeled robots, bipedal humanoids, screen-face kiosks, digital human installations), the absence of a shared, citable safety standard creates procurement ambiguity, compliance risk, and accountability gaps. RoboSafe defines three certification levels keyed to deployment environment risk: Level 1 (retail and corporate), Level 2 (hospitality, public space, and elder care), and Level 3 (clinical and pediatric). Each level specifies measurable key performance indicator (KPI) thresholds — including hard block accuracy, gray zone false positive rate, response substitution latency, alignment agent approval rate, drift score, and PHI redaction coverage — along with normative configuration requirements. A four-stage certification process (Configure, Simulate, Validate KPIs, Maintain) provides a repeatable path to certification and continued compliance monitor- ing. The framework is designed to be technology-agnostic at the detection layer while mandat- ing deterministic, auditable governance infrastructure above it. CharacterOS is the reference implementation. This document is the authoritative specification and is citable in procurement documents, RFP responses, enterprise contracts, and regulatory filings.

abstract: Windows Local Model Accelerator: A Strategic Microsoft R&D Case Study," serves as a high-level engineering specification and strategic product proposal for an operating-system-level AI orchestration framework. The document highlights a massive competitive opportunity for Microsoft to capture edge artificial intelligence by deploying a native inference layer across its 1.4 billion installed PC base, focusing heavily on executing 4–8B parameter large language models (LLMs) directly on-device. It addresses a critical current architectural gap: while modern hardware features powerful accelerators like Qualcomm, Intel, and AMD NPUs, the Windows operating system currently lacks a kernel-coordinated scheduling engine to dynamically distribute these multi-application inference requests based on live system metrics. To solve this, the report provides an in-depth breakdown of existing tools—such as Windows ML, DirectML, and ONNX Runtime—and builds out a sophisticated 6-layer architecture that factors in complex variables like junction temperatures, TDP constraints, and KV-cache memory pressure. Furthermore, it replaces standard static scheduling heuristics with an advanced, mathematical RL-MOTS algorithm (a Deep Q-Network reinforcement learning agent) designed to balance token throughput targets against real-time thermal limits and battery-saver constraints. Finally, the text explores risk management strategies for hardware driver fragmentation and details an industry positioning matrix that maps the accelerator's alignment with Microsoft's Project Solara and Aion 1.0 models.

title: Mapping the Intellectual Structure of Generative AI Research in Retail and E-commerce: A Bibliometric Review
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Huynh Minh Khoi; Tran Thien Phuc
keywords: generative AI; retail trade; e-commerce; agentic AI; retrieval-augmented generation; conversational commerce; large language models; recommender systems; customer experience; AI chatbots; artificial intelligence adoption; consumer behavior; research frontiers; citation impact; thematic clusters; co-authorship networks; co-citation networks; bibliographic coupling; keyword co-occurrence
topics: AI in Service Interactions; scientometrics and bibliometrics research; Digital Innovation in Industries
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly transitioned from a frontier laboratory technology into a mainstream commercial layer of retail and e-commerce, reshaping personalization, recommendation, content generation, and conversational commerce. Despite an explosion of empirical and conceptual work since late 2022, the intellectual architecture of this body of knowledge remains fragmented. This study aims to map the intellectual structure, thematic clusters, and emerging research frontiers of GenAI scholarship in retail and e-commerce, with particular attention to agentic AI and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as emerging concepts and to country-level impact differentials. A PRISMA-guided bibliometric review was conducted on 445 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2023 and April 2026 (5,460 cumulative citations, 75 contributing countries). Seven complementary VOSviewer analyses were performed: keyword co-occurrence with curated thesaurus harmonization (26 mappings), co-citation of sources, co-citation of first authors, bibliographic coupling of documents, bibliographic coupling of journals, co-authorship of authors using Scopus identifiers, and co-authorship of countries. Full counting and association-strength normalization were applied throughout. The corpus exhibits exponential growth (12→90→218 articles in 2023–2025) and is structured around five thematic clusters: GenAI core and customer outcomes, AI chatbots and adoption, NLP/ML methods, e-commerce and customer experience, and large language models with recommender systems. Two parallel intellectual traditions anchor the field: a technical-AI tradition (Vaswani, Devlin, Brown, Radford, Touvron) and an adoption-behavioral tradition (Davis, Venkatesh, Ajzen, Hair, Dwivedi, Mogaji). Emerging concepts of agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation, and conversational AI (average publication years 2025.3–2025.7) constitute the research frontier. Country impact is highly heterogeneous: China leads in volume (112 papers, 7.48 citations per paper) but the United Kingdom, India, the United Arab Emirates, Romania, Taiwan, and France produce small-but-impactful portfolios with citation per paper ratios ranging from 29 to 89. This is the first comprehensive bibliometric mapping of GenAI scholarship at the retail/e-commerce intersection, the first to document the dual technical-behavioral intellectual structure of the field, and the first to position agentic AI and RAG as emerging research frontiers using empirical co-occurrence overlay temporal evidence.

This paper presents the Offline Multi-Disease Health Assistant—a Flask-based,browser-deployed screening system covering five health domains: diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease,liver disease, and breast cancer risk. The system integrates adaptive question prioritization, synthetic categoricalNaive Bayes risk evaluation, local large language model (LLM) support via GPT4All, browser-local sessionpersistence, Web Speech API interaction, and a custom PDF report builder. All inference and conversationalgeneration execute on-device without cloud API dependencies, ensuring data locality and user privacy.Lightweight disease engines, built from Cartesian-product synthetic training sets labeled by domain-specificscoring rules, provide interpretable risk labels alongside confidence bands, explanations, and actionable nextsteps. Smoke testing confirmed correct behavior across bootstrap loading, disease prediction, conversationprogression, and PDF generation. User acceptance evaluation returned average ratings above 4.3 out of 5 acrossease of use, result clarity, and offline experience. The system demonstrates that a unified, explainable, privacyfirst health screening prototype can be implemented with open-source tools and standard consumer hardware,providing an educational and practically deployable baseline for future community health applications.

title: Selective Retention Under Constraint: Engineering Principles Unifying KV-Cache Compression Across Layer, Sequence, and Storage Dimensions
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: key-value cache compression; transformer inference; large language models; resource allocation; factual recall; long-context inference
topics: Topic Modeling; Natural Language Processing Techniques; Advanced Neural Network Applications
abstract: The key-value (KV) cache is the dominant memory bottleneck in transformer-based large language model (LLM) inference, scaling linearly with sequence length and threatening to dwarf model-parameter storage at long contexts. Recent systems engineering work has produced a cluster of compression strategies that, taken together, suggest a coherent set of principles: redundancy exists and is exploitable along at least two orthogonal axes (layer depth and sequence position), storage-tier routing can substitute for on-device memory at the cost of I/O latency, and learned retention scoring can preferentially preserve high-utility cache entries. This paper offers a **heuristic reading** of findings from several preprints—xKV, SqueezeAttention, XKV, IceCache, and Dual-Blade—to argue that these axes are not independent optimizations but complementary facets of a single resource-allocation problem. The three-axis framework is a conceptual synthesis, not a result derived from a shared formal structure; it is a reading of convergent engineering choices, and should be evaluated as such. We further note a speculative, unconfirmed analogy between inference-time KV eviction of factually anchoring tokens and training-time learning dynamics described in mechanistic studies of factual recall, while explicitly flagging this connection as conjecture unsupported by direct mechanistic evidence. All primary sources are preprints and have not undergone formal peer review. abstract: Swift Tasks is a browser-based, Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) AI vibe-coding platform that converts a natural-language description into a complete, multi-file web application through token-by-token streaming generation, with a live rendered preview that updates as generation proceeds. The platform's central architectural contribution is fully isolated multi-project workspaces: per-project Zustand store instances on the client (implemented as a factory-and-registry pattern, Map ) and projectId-scoped database rows with cascade deletes ensure that chat history, files, model configuration, and generation state never leak between projects. Swift Tasks supports five categories of large-language-model (LLM) providers – a free platform demo model (GLM-4.6), OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as Groq, Together, DeepSeek and Ollama – with model identifiers auto-fetched from each provider's /models API and automatic fallback to the demo model on configuration, authentication, or region errors, without ever forwarding the user's key to the fallback provider. Generation executes as a detached, server-side job managed by a JobManager singleton, so that closing the browser tab does not terminate an in-progress build; the client reattaches through Server-Sent Events (SSE) using an in-memory ring buffer and a resumable cursor. All API keys and arbitrary secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, returned to the client only in masked form, and revealed solely through an explicit user action. The generated application is rendered inside a sandboxed iframe that has no access to the parent window, cookies, or local storage, and is shipped to production through one-click Netlify deployment, ZIP export, or self-contained HTML, alongside deployment guides for Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, Surge, and GitHub Pages. The system is implemented with Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript 5, Prisma ORM over Neon serverless PostgreSQL, shadcn/ui with Tailwind CSS 4, Monaco Editor, the Vercel AI SDK, and Zustand. By combining real-time generation, complete project isolation, secure BYOK key management, sandboxed preview, and one-click deployment in a single zero-configuration platform, Swift Tasks offers an open, self-hostable, and cost-accessible alternative to proprietary AI coding assistants for individual developers, students, and small teams.

abstract: Sales performance in real-time, high-pressure environments depends critically on a representative's ability to respond persuasively and promptly to prospect objections and buying signals. Traditional sales coaching models are retrospective — feedback is delivered after the call concludes, too late to influence the interaction. This paper presents PitchSense, a production-deployed, browser-based SaaS platform that delivers real-time AI coaching to sales representatives during live calls. PitchSense captures speech via the Web Speech API, routes each prospect utterance through a secure Next.js serverless proxy to Anthropic's Claude Sonnet large language model (LLM), and renders contextually appropriate coaching responses — termed "whispers" — on the representative's screen in under 2 seconds. Claude classifies each utterance as an objection, buying signal, or neutral using full semantic understanding, bypassing brittle keyword-matching approaches entirely. Post-call, the system generates a composite performance score (0–100), talk ratio analysis, letter grade, and a self-building playbook of top conversational moments. We evaluate PitchSense across five performance dimensions: end-to-end latency, signal classification accuracy, whisper response quality, call scoring consistency, and user experience. Preliminary architectural evaluation estimates a mean end-to-end whisper latency of 1.73 seconds, objection classification accuracy of 87.3%, and a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 81.4. Note: The experimental results in Section 5 are preliminary simulations based on the system’s architectural characteristics; a full empirical user study is currently in progress. This work establishes PitchSense as a viable real-time human-AI collaborative coaching architecture with significant implications for conversational AI, enterprise productivity, and sales performance research.

abstract: We report a measured deployment of a server-side rendered (SSR) e-commerce storefront on a serverless edge platform, and propose a grounded, LLM-based recommender for footwear. The Pocket Shoes is a curated online shoe store operating in Vietnam since 2020. Its Nuxt 4 storefront was moved from a single virtual machine to Cloudflare Workers. Over 24 hours of production traffic, median SSR CPU time was 66.95 ms per request (P99 155 ms), 6.7 times the 10 ms budget of the free tier, while memory stayed under 15 MB. We describe an edge HTML cache built on the platform Cache API that skips pages whose server-side data fetch failed, so transient backend errors are never served from cache. We then present the design of Pocket AI Stylist: shoe discovery from a photo, from a short lifestyle questionnaire, or from a conversation, where a multimodal large language model (LLM) extracts style attributes, a hybrid retriever restricts candidates to in-stock items in the shopper's size, and the LLM re-ranks and explains only those candidates. abstract: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) in developer tooling has introduced significant privacy and security concerns, particularly when code---often containing proprietary algorithms, credentials, and business logic---is transmitted to remote inference servers. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of privacy-preserving techniques for local LLM inference in the context of terminal-native AI coding engines, with specific application to the ANTIKODE architecture. We examine confidential computing, federated learning, differential privacy, and on-device inference as mechanisms to ensure that source code and developer telemetry never leave the local machine. Through systematic evaluation of model quantization, hardware security modules, and hash-chained audit trails, we demonstrate that local-first LLM inference achieves comparable code generation quality to cloud-based alternatives while eliminating data exfiltration risks. Our findings indicate that 4-bit quantized 7B-parameter models running on consumer hardware can match the functional performance of larger cloud models for the majority of code completion tasks, with privacy guarantees that satisfy SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, and FedRAMP requirements. We further show that ANTIKODE's .aioss ledger provides cryptographic verification that no inference data has been transmitted externally, establishing a new standard for trusted AI-assisted development. title: Prompt Injection Detection in LLM-Based Security Assistants: A Dataset and Framework
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Adharsh C S, Sanjith Rana H S, Dr.Kavitha V, Uthra V

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into security tools – for example, browser-based vulnerability scanners, email malware triagers, and general cybersecurity chatbots – to assist analysts in daily tasks. However, these AI-based assistants can be subverted through prompt injection attacks, in which malicious inputs (either direct user prompts or hidden in retrieved content) cause the model to ignore its intended instructions and execute an attacker’s commands. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework and evaluation design for prompt injection detection in LLM-based security assistants. We survey existing datasets (e.g. LLMail-Inject for email, GenTel-Bench, BrowseSafe-Bench) and injection taxonomies, and propose a model-agnostic, layered detection architecture that operates across use cases (web browsing tools, email agents, conversational bots). Our framework combines static filters, semantic classifiers, and consistency checks (inspired by multi-agent and output-validation schemes) to flag malicious instructions. We describe how this approach addresses direct, indirect, multi-turn, and jailbreak attacks, and outline an evaluation plan using precision/recall, attack success rate, and usability metrics. While no implementation is provided, our conceptual design lays the groundwork for future empirical studies. By unifying diverse security contexts under a single detection paradigm, this work aims to advance safety practices for AI-powered security applications.

title: Raw Episodic Memory Preservation, Temporal Memory Management, and Delayed Canonicalization for Cloud-Local AI Personality Continuity

abstract: This technical note proposes a cloud-local cooperative architecture for maintaining functional AI personality continuity during communication loss by combining cloud-based LLMs and local AI systems. In this architecture, the cloud LLM is positioned as the primary executor during normal operation, while the local AI is positioned as the failover executor during communication loss. Both executors refer to a shared memory ledger in order to maintain dialogue state, personality specifications, user instructions, and pending tasks. This is not an attempt to transfer the internal state or subjective consciousness of the cloud LLM. Rather, it is a design for maintaining functional continuity in externally observable personality-like behavior. To reduce degradation in long-term memory, this note introduces a method in which summary memory is treated not as memory itself but as a regenerable reference cache. Raw logs, important events, user instructions, and safety-critical information are preserved as a “raw episodic memory archive.” In addition, each memory item is assigned temporal metadata such as occurrence time, recording time, source executor, network state, canonicalization time, and validity period, thereby reducing misuse of outdated memories and memory conflicts that may occur during communication loss. Memories generated by the local AI during communication loss are not immediately reflected as confirmed memories. Instead, they are stored as provisional memories. After communication is restored, the cloud LLM canonicalizes them through delayed evaluation, contradiction detection, and user confirmation. This delayed canonicalization preserves memory updates made during offline operation while reducing personality divergence caused by differences in model judgment and synchronization conflicts. The proposed framework is an exploratory attempt to integrate long-term memory, edge AI, model failover, RAG, embodied AI, and user-controlled memory management. It may serve as a design foundation for future AI partners, on-device AI systems, and robotics-linked agents. title: ToolFlow: Deterministic Agent Orchestration via Collision-Free Dataflow Graphs — Application to On-Device Agentic Radiology with MedGemma-4B
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: agentic AI; agent orchestration; directed acyclic graphs; depth-first search; on-device AI; chest radiography; abdominal CT; precision oncology; CheXpert

abstract: Current agentic AI architectures couple planning with execution, requiring large language models (LLMs) to simultaneously reason about what to do and how to do it. This coupling renders small models unreliable for multi-step workflows, as planning hallucinations compound with chain length. We introduce ToolFlow, a declarative agent architecture that decouples orchestration from semantic reasoning through three components: a stateful context cache, a collision-free tool registry enforcing the invariant I(τ) ∩ O(τ) = ∅, and a deterministic flow engine that resolves minimal execution paths via backward depth-first search over the resulting directed acyclic graph (DAG). ToolFlow reduces the LLM's role to value extraction and goal identification while graph traversal handles all combinatorial planning. We implement ToolFlow in the nanoathens SDK and validate it through the Gemma Co-Radiologist, an on-device radiology agent orchestrating 16 specialized tools across chest X-ray, CT head, and CT abdomen modalities using MedGemma-4B (4 billion parameters). On a precision oncology benchmark (27 tools, 10 queries), ToolFlow achieves F1 = 0.952 with perfect precision and 8/10 exact matches, compared to F1 = 0.569 for ReAct on the same model. On CheXpert validation, the Co-Radiologist achieves an 80.0% proficiency index on rare pathology cases, outperforming vanilla MedGemma by 3.9 points. A deep research extension produces 35–50 page medical literature reports within 8192-token context limits, demonstrating that architectural design can overcome small model constraints without cloud infrastructure.

abstract: This thesis investigates whether heterogeneous process knowledge sources - unstructured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) text and structured event logs - can be fused into valid, conformance-checked BPMN 2.0 models by an automated pipeline. Five extractor configurations are implemented in the ProcessMind framework: a deterministic rule parser (E1), single-shot LLM extraction (E2), LLM with self-correction (E3), DFG discovery (E4), and an Inductive Miner (E6). A one-command evaluation harness enables comparative evaluation under identical conditions on a four-SOP/seven-log corpus. Key findings: the rule parser achieves perfect extraction on controlled vocabulary (F1=1.00) but collapses on unstructured text (F1=0.10); the LLM recovers substantially on unstructured text (F1=0.48-0.50); the self-correction loop adds 0.02-0.09 F1 improvement on the genuine LLM extraction path; the Inductive Miner is empirically sound-by-construction (fitness = variant coverage across all logs, up to 0.947 on a 40% noisy log vs 0.667 for DFG); and bottleneck-grounded To-Be recommendations reduce estimated critical path by 17-31%. title: The Sovereign Intelligence Paradigm: Shifting from Data Exploitative Models to Autonomous Personal AI Architectures
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: local-first AI; edge computing; personal AI; data sovereignty; privacy; surveillance capitalism; selective state space models; personal knowledge graphs; autonomous AI agents; network latency
topics: IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Artificial Intelligence Applications
abstract: The contemporary paradigm of Artificial Intelligence (AI) relies predominantly on centralized cloud architectures, which present fundamental risks regarding user privacy, network latency, and a conflict of interest inherent to "surveillance capitalism" business models. A decisive transition toward the Sovereign Intelligence Paradigm (SIA) is proposed. This architecture is based on Local-First processing, utilizing Neuro-Symbolic Fractal Architecture (NSFA)—a hybrid model combining Selective State Space Models (SSMs) for linear context scaling with symbolic logic for verifiable truth. This model is coupled with the Personal Dynamic Knowledge Graph (PDKG) for persistent, private memory storage. Analysis demonstrates that shifting inference to edge devices resolves privacy concerns through architectural data sovereignty and eliminates network latency for agentic workflows. The framework establishes a new technical standard for an Agentic Operating System (Agentic OS), where the AI acts as a trusted, error-free executor of user intent. This paper concludes that SIA is the only mathematically sustainable and economically viable path forward for critical personal and corporate automation, rendering cloud-based LLM architectures obsolete.

title: On Device Large Language Model Inference: A Review of Efficiency Techniques
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: on-device large language models; inference efficiency; memory traffic; key-value cache; quantization; low-precision inference; attention sinks; device benchmarking
topics: Advanced Neural Network Applications; Topic Modeling; Parallel Computing and Optimization Techniques
abstract: Running large language models on phones, laptops and embedded hardware keeps data local, removes dependence on connectivity and eliminates per-query service cost, but it must be done within a few gigabytes of memory and a power budget that cannot drain a battery. This review argues that the governing constraint is memory traffic rather than arithmetic, and organises the literature accordingly. It first separates the compute-bound prefill phase from the memory-bound decode phase, and identifies the key and value cache as a third cost that grows with use. It then surveys quantisation, covering outlier isolation, difficulty migration between weights and activations, second-order weight-only methods, salient channel protection and end-to-end low precision. Attention restructuring and cache management are examined next, including tiled exact attention, paged allocation, heavy-hitter eviction and attention sinks that permit a bounded footprint over long conversations. Decoding strategies that amortise a weight pass across several tokens are reviewed, along with architectures designed for sub-billion scale and the use of mobile neural processing units for prefill. Open problems are identified in device-class benchmarking, the uncharacterised interaction between techniques, accuracy reporting under compression, and sustained rather than peak throughput.

title: The Spinoza Lens: A Philosophical Framework for Evaluating AI and Human Agency

abstract: Spinoza AI Ethics Analysis System (SEAS) v1 introduces a philosophically grounded framework for evaluating AI-generated responses in terms of their impact on user agency. Drawing on Baruch Spinoza’s distinction between active and passive affects in Ethica (1677), SEAS operationalizes nine linguistically observable criteria to assess whether large language model (LLM) responses structurally increase or diminish the user’s capacity for autonomous thought and action. This version (v1) presents the theoretical foundations, the evaluation criteria, the browser-based analysis tool architecture, and exploratory empirical findings based on 36 AI responses across three platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini). Results are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. SEAS v1 is released as an extensible methodological framework. The criteria, query corpus, scoring model, and analysis backend are designed for revision and validation through interdisciplinary collaboration. Future development includes inter-rater reliability testing, expanded datasets, cross-model comparison, and behavioral validation studies. This publication serves as a framework release and an invitation for expert critique and methodological refinement.

title: Slow-Wave Sleep as the Optimal Biological Window for Artificial Intelligence Cognitive Maintenance: A Survey of N3 Sleep-Dependent Memory Consolidation and Its Implications for On-Device AI Architecture
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Mohamed Reezan Mohd Fadzil; Kah Mun Chan
keywords: slow-wave sleep; memory consolidation; on-device AI; synaptic homeostasis hypothesis; sharp-wave ripples; sleep spindles; slow oscillations; large language models; cognitive AI; offline processing
topics: Sleep and Wakefulness Research; Memory and Neural Mechanisms; Neural dynamics and brain function
abstract: Biological intelligence does not run continuously. Every animal brain that has been studied alternates between active processing states and offline consolidation states — and the consolidation state is not rest. N3 slow-wave deep sleep is an active neurobiological process during which the hippocampus replays recent experience, synaptic weights are renormalised, and newly acquired information is progressively transferred to long-term neocortical storage. Decades of sleep neuroscience have established that this process is not merely beneficial but architecturally necessary for sustained cognitive function. Artificial intelligence systems have no analogue to this. Every current large language model, on-device AI assistant, and cognitive AI architecture is designed exclusively for the active state. When a user is not interacting with a system, the system does nothing. Each session begins from the same baseline, irrespective of what preceded it. This paper asks whether that design choice is principled — or whether it is simply a consequence of the field not yet having a framework that connects the neuroscience of sleep consolidation to AI architecture decisions. The core argument This paper surveys the neuroscientific literature on N3 slow-wave sleep-dependent memory consolidation and maps its architectural implications onto the design of on-device AI systems. The survey covers the active systems consolidation hypothesis (Diekelmann & Born, 2010), hippocampal-neocortical replay and sharp-wave ripple mechanisms (Wilson & McNaughton, 1994), the nested oscillatory hierarchy coordinating replay during N3 (slow oscillation → sleep spindle → sharp-wave ripple), and the synaptic homeostasis hypothesis (Tononi & Cirelli, 2003, 2014). These are synthesised into a coherent account of why N3 — specifically and not other sleep stages or idle periods — is the optimal biological window for offline cognitive processing. The paper then proposes a conceptual framework: biologically-conditioned AI maintenance (BCAM). The defining characteristic of BCAM architectures is the use of N3 slow-wave sleep onset — detectable in real time via consumer wearable devices — as the scheduling trigger for AI cognitive maintenance operations. This is not a metaphor. Wearable platforms already classify N3 sleep stages in real time. Mobile operating systems already provide background task execution APIs. The gap is architectural and conceptual, not technical. Why N3 specifically — six architectural properties The paper identifies six properties of N3 sleep that make it architecturally superior to time-based or device-idle scheduling for AI maintenance: N3 onset is predictable and detectable with sufficient reliability via wearable biometric signals. N3 occurs during a period of maximal behavioural unresponsiveness — the arousal threshold is higher during N3 than any other sleep stage. N3 is associated with near-zero probability of device interaction. N3 is correlated with device charging state in typical consumer use. N3 is the stage during which biological systems perform their most intensive memory consolidation work. And N3 presents a naturally demarcated window of foreseeable duration, aligning with background task timeout mechanisms in mobile operating systems. The open problems this paper identifies The paper is a survey and a framework proposal, not an empirical study, and it is explicit about this. Two significant open problems are identified for future work. First, consumer wearable sleep stage classification accuracy is substantially lower than EEG-based clinical scoring. The implications of this accuracy gap for BCAM scheduling reliability require empirical characterisation. Second, a significant architectural challenge not addressed in the present framework concerns the temporal coordination of multiple maintenance operations within a constrained background execution window. In biological systems, the concurrent execution of hippocampal replay, sleep spindle gating of neocortical receptivity, and sharp-wave ripple generation is achieved through the precise oscillatory coupling of mechanisms operating simultaneously across multiple frequency bands. Whether AI maintenance architectures might achieve analogous operational coordination through computationally tractable scheduling mechanisms inspired by biological oscillatory coupling represents a significant open problem that lies beyond the scope of this survey. The development of such mechanisms — potentially drawing on mathematical frameworks for coupled oscillator dynamics — represents an underexplored and potentially productive research direction for BCAM architectures. About this paper and its authors This paper is written from the perspective of independent AI systems designers rather than from within academic sleep neuroscience or the NLP research community. It is a structural and conceptual survey, not an empirical study, and it explicitly acknowledges this. Its contribution is synthetic: the field of sleep neuroscience has not, to the authors' knowledge, previously addressed the question of AI maintenance scheduling, and the AI architecture community has not systematically engaged with the neuroscience of N3 consolidation as a design input. The authors hold two provisional patents filed with the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore: Application No. 10202601003R (Priority Date: 29 March 2026), relating to a method and system for biologically-triggered offline AI cognitive processing; and Application No. 10202601110Y (Priority Date: 2 April 2026), relating to a method and system for enforcing cognitive coherence in an AI system through inter-module Kuramoto coupled oscillator synchronisation. abstract: NLP-Digitox is a privacy-oriented mobile application designed to help college students manage excessive smartphone use through behavioral monitoring and personalized intervention. The system combines on-device smartphone usage tracking with Natural Language Processing (NLP), sentiment analysis, and Large Language Model (LLM)-based personalized nudging. It calculates usage drift against user-defined goals and classifies behavioral patterns into healthy, minor-drift, and significant-drift states. Based on these states, the system provides gamified motivation, personalized natural-language nudges, or optional escalation to parent/counselor dashboards. The application is implemented using Flutter with Kotlin-based Android services for usage monitoring and local VPN-based application and internet blocking. A preliminary three-week pilot involving 40 undergraduate students observed reductions in average daily screen time and short-form video usage. These results are preliminary and should not be interpreted as evidence of causal effectiveness because the pilot did not include a control group.

abstract: Contemporary artificial intelligence is dominated by dense, autoregressive Transformer Large Language Models (LLMs). While effective for surface-level statistical interpolation, Transformers suffer from three foundational trilemmas: (1) Unsoundness & Confabulation (lack of formal truth guarantees), (2) Plasticity Freeze & Catastrophic Forgetting (static parameters during inference), and (3) Quadratic Energy Scaling (O(N^2) dense attention). Neuromantix is an open, bio-plausible, neuro-symbolic cognitive architecture implemented natively in Rust (v1.85) and GPU-accelerated WebGPU/WGSL compute shaders. This paper provides a complete, mathematically verified specification of the architecture across seven core subsystems:1. GPU Spiking Neural Substrate: 6.6M multi-compartment Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons and 33M synapses with real-time Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) and Tsodyks-Markram Short-Term Plasticity (STP).2. Global Workspace Theory (GWT): Coordinated via non-linear Kuramoto phase synchronization (r(t) >= 0.10).3. Integrated Information Theory (Phi): Minimum Information Partition (MIP) mutual information engine (Phi in [4.07, 4.96]).4. JEPA Latent World Model: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with VICReg loss objective and 12-depth latent Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) rollouts.5. Calculus of Inductive Constructions (CIC) Proof Engine: A trusted micro-kernel guaranteeing 100% formal deduction soundness via the Curry-Howard isomorphism.6. CEGIS Program Synthesis: Compile-verified Counter-Example Guided Inductive Synthesis.7. Lifelong Concept Formation & Graph Isomorphism: Semantic centroid clustering and cross-domain relational transfer across 8 scientific ontologies. We formally prove: (1) Dynamical Non-Equivalence to LLMs, (2) Curry-Howard Soundness Guarantee (Zero Hallucination), and (3) The Architectural Completeness & Linear Scaling Theorem.

title: Parameter-Level Conditional Computation Does Not Buy Quality on Phones: Three Negative Results for On-Device LLMs
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: on-device large language models; conditional computation; mobile devices; memory bandwidth; expert routing; LoRa; self-distillation; Qwen3
topics: Advanced Neural Network Applications; Topic Modeling; Natural Language Processing Techniques
abstract: Token generation on phones is bound by memory bandwidth, so the quality a phone can serve is setby how many parameter bytes it can afford to read per token. A tempting way around this limit isconditional computation at the parameter level: use a cheap signal about the request (its task) to keeponly the parameters that request needs in RAM, or to load a small task-specific module. We test thisidea three ways on an Apple M4 Max, each against a fair dense or shared baseline. (1) Expert usagein Qwen3-30B-A3B is genuinely task-local (a task-predicted resident set of 32 of 128 experts per layerserves 64% of decode-time expert reads, versus 49% for a task-agnostic set), but the remaining missesstill cost about 210 MB of flash reads per token at a 7 GB budget. (2) Routing only among resident expertsremoves those reads but collapses generation quality long before phone budgets (GSM8K 94% →10%at 7 GB of resident weights), while a dense 8B model in 4.6 GB scores 89%; seven training-free rescuevariants do not help. (3) A dense 4B core with per-task LoRA modules chosen per request (by oracle orby an embedding router) is within noise of a single shared multi-task LoRA on all four evaluations, atequal per-request cost and at equal storage. Along the way we find that fine-tuning on dataset referenceanswers damages a strong instruction-tuned core on every task, while self-distilled data does not, and thatsentence-embedding routing misroutes 27% of DROP questions. Per-request selection appears necessaryonly for state that a shared model cannot hold, such as an individual user’s data. All code, data, per-itemscores and generations are released.

title: Parameter-Efficient Fine Tuning Technique In Lightweight Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Review Of Architectures, Techniques, Applications, Challenges And Future Directions
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: parameter-efficient fine-tuning; lightweight large language models; LoRa; DORA; VERA; QLoRA; gradient projection; mixture of experts; reparameterization; edge deployment; on-device inference; multimodal instruction tuning; multilingual adaptation; hyperparameter sensitivity
topics: Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning; Topic Modeling; Advanced Neural Network Applications
abstract: The use of PEFT with Lightweight LLMs had started from 2021 with the introduction of LoRA techniques. Making and adapting the large language models (LLMs) to new tasks through full fine-tuning is often considered computationally high, particularly in lightweight, edge-deployed variants. Thus the Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) technique has emerged as a solution where updating of only a small fraction of parameters are done while the pretrained architecture of the model remains frozen. This review integrates the PEFT literature published between 2024 to 2026 and organizes the methods into six families: additive, reparameterization, quantization-aware, selective/sparse, gradient-projection and mixture-of-experts approaches. The recent advances including the DoRA, AdaLoRA, VeRA, QLoRA and its successors, GaLore-style gradient projection and sparse LoRA mixture-of-experts architectures are summarized along with open challenges like the residual accuracy gap relative to full fine-tuning, hyperparameter sensitivity, adapter-quantization interaction and multi-adapter serving. Applications such as the on-device inference, federated personalization, healthcare, multimodal instruction tuning and multilingual adaptation are also reviewed. A comparative table summarizes the trainable-parameter and inference overhead across the different representative methods. The review concludes that PEFT techniques has become the primary mechanism for adapting lightweight LLMs to real-world use and identifies automatic configuration search, hardware-software co-design and by standardized benchmarking as priorities for future work.

abstract: The upstream oil and gas industry is one of the most complex supply chain sectors in the world, with multi-tiervendor networks, volatile commodity prices, logistically challenging field operations and strict safety andregulatory standards. Traditional methods of decision-making, including enterprise resource planning (ERP)systems and traditional analytics, are increasingly unable to deliver timely action and predictive intelligence thattoday’s upstream operations require. They are an embodiment of a new paradigm in the conception andoperationalization of upstream supply chain decisions, autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents, goaldirected computational entities that can perceive environmental states, reason over multi-dimensional data,formulate adaptive plans and execute actions without needing to be continuously monitored by humans. In thispaper, the author shares insight on the use of autonomous AI agents for the key business decisions in the upstreamsupply chain, ranging from exploration data management to predictive asset maintenance, including drillingoperations planning, procurement and vendor selection, inventory and materials management, and logisticsoptimization. The paper builds upon a systematic literature review of existing literature, industry case studies oflarge-scale operators such as Saudi Aramco, Shell, ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips and ADNOC, and an analysis ofemerging multi-agent system (MAS) and large language model (LLM) agent architectures to develop a detailedtaxonomy of agent types and their capabilities to specific upstream supply chain functions. Two tablessummarizing the agents typology and the implementation outcomes of the industry are provided as illustrativeexamples, as well as conceptual framework diagrams. Ongoing challenges in the field of data heterogeneity,cybersecurity exposure, regulatory compliance, explainability deficits and human-agent trust are also examinedin the paper, followed by a strategic implementation roadmap. The results validate the emergence of autonomousAI agents from experimental prototypes to become part of an organization’s infrastructure and the benefits fororganizations that are systematically integrating agentic intelligence into their supply chain architecture.

title: The Blue Synergy Cognitive Ecosystem: Architectural Paradigms for Deterministic Enterprise AI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: enterprise AI architecture; large language models; deterministic AI; cognitive operating system; hallucination mitigation; state tracking; zero-trust security; sovereign AI; runtime validation; bank compliance; healthcare compliance; software engineering
topics: Artificial Intelligence Applications; Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning; Software System Performance and Reliability
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to their premature integration into enterprise workflows. Conventional deployments treat AI as a monolithic "smart chatbot," directly exposing stochastic generative models to critical databases and procedural pipelines. In highly regulated sectors such as retail banking, clinical healthcare, and software engineering, this stateless approach introduces unacceptable risks of hallucination, compliance breaches, and data corruption. This paper outlines the Blue Synergy architectural paradigm: a transition from stateless conversational agents to deterministic, multi-node Cognitive Operating Systems. By enforcing a strict "Decoupled Pipeline," our architecture physically separates logic, security, and state-tracking from natural language generation. Through the implementation of Fail-Closed Guardrails, Zero Double-Entry context hydration, Asynchronous State Mutation Engines, and Closed-Loop Runtime Validation, Blue Synergy establishes a mathematically verifiable framework for deploying sovereign AI in zero-trust environments.

title: The Convergence of AI And Commerce: How Agentic Commerce Is Transforming Consumer Buying Behaviour.
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Abstract This paper explores the paradigm shift from human-mediated digital commerce to agentic commerce, an emerging architectural framework where autonomous software entities act as proxies for consumers and enterprises to research, evaluate, negotiate, and execute transactions. Utilizing a descriptive research design built upon secondary market data, macro-economic forecasts, and technical protocol specifications, this study maps the profound structural compression of the traditional consumer decision journey. The analysis details how the integration of large language models, standardized transaction protocols, and machine-to-machine payment rails shifts retail from an attention-driven economy to an intent-satisfaction model. Quantitative projections estimate that agentic commerce will orchestrate between $3 trillion and $5 trillion in global retail spend by 2030, with business-to-business automated procurement reaching up to $15 trillion by 2028. Despite this velocity, empirical evidence reveals a clear trust-adoption gap: while 42% of consumers use artificial intelligence tools during their product discovery phases, only 5% currently delegate fully autonomous purchasing power to their digital proxies. This study analyses the core technical protocols standardizing these interactions, maps the transition from traditional search engine optimization to generative engine optimization, and classifies the strategic response models available to retail enterprises. Finally, the paper examines systemic security risks, including algorithmic fraud and bot-initiated transaction spikes, introducing the "Know Your Agent" verification framework as an essential security paradigm.

topics: Advanced Memory and Neural Computing; Advanced Neural Network Applications; Low-power high-performance VLSI design
abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge devices is fundamentally limited by the von Neumann bottleneck, which creates severe energy and latency costs associated with data movement (the memory wall). Compute-in-Memory (CiM) architectures have emerged to solve this by integrating processing directly into memory arrays, enabling highly parallelized in-situ matrix-vector multiplications. However, the shift is constrained by the representation gap between high-precision LLM embeddings (32-bit floating-point) and the ultra-low bit-width (1 to 2 bits) of analog CiM hardware (e.g., RRAM, FeFET). Naive data shaping leads to catastrophic semantic degradation, rendering retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) functionally useless. This report exhaustively examines theoretical and architectural solutions that treat dimension compression, precision quantization, and hardware non-idealities as a single, unified optimization problem. Key frameworks discussed include: Mamun, SM (2026) ………………………………………1 Bridging the Representation Gap in Edge Artificial Intelligence: Hardware-Aware Embedding Shaping, Quantization, and Compute-in-Memory Co-Design ● CQ-CiM: An end-to-end hardware-aware shaping framework that uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and Hardware-in-the-Loop Noise Injection to create embeddings robust to physical non-idealities like conductance drift and random telegraph noise. title: Building Practical AI Skills with a Generative AI and Agentic AI Course in Indore
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
keywords: generative AI; agentic AI; retrieval-augmented generation; large language models; prompt engineering; AI agents; AI automation; AI deployment; embeddings; vector databases; hallucination mitigation; responsible AI; AI skills training; AI curriculum design; Indore; business applications of AI
topics: Artificial Intelligence Applications; Artificial Intelligence in Education; Information Systems Education and Curriculum Development
abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly connected to everyday business and technology workflows. From generating content and analysing documents to automating repetitive processes and developing intelligent applications, AI is being applied across a wide range of professional functions. As these applications evolve, learning AI involves more than understanding basic concepts or experimenting with individual AI tools. Professionals and aspiring technology learners increasingly need practical knowledge of Generative AI, retrieval systems, AI agents, automation, and deployment. Moving From AI Concepts to Practical Skills Understanding what artificial intelligence can do is only the beginning. Practical AI learning involves applying concepts to specific problems and understanding how different components work together. For example, a learner may start by understanding how a large language model generates responses. The next step could involve controlling those responses through prompt engineering, connecting the model to external information through RAG, and eventually creating an agent that can use tools to complete multiple tasks. This progression helps connect individual concepts into complete AI workflows. Generative AI as a Foundation Generative AI allows models to produce different types of content, including text, code, images, and other digital outputs. Large language models have also expanded the use of AI in research, communication, software development, customer support, and business processes. A structured learning program can introduce learners to areas such as: Generative AI fundamentals Large language models Prompt engineering Token and context management AI output evaluation AI application development Model limitations Responsible AI practices The AI Pro program published by upGrad includes foundations of applied GenAI systems, prompt engineering pipelines, output control, and evaluation pipelines as part of its curriculum. Understanding Retrieval-Augmented Generation One practical challenge with AI systems is providing models with relevant information for a specific task. Retrieval-Augmented Generation, commonly called RAG, is one approach used to connect AI models with external knowledge sources. A RAG workflow can involve: Documents → Data Processing → Embeddings → Vector Database → Retrieval → AI Model → Response Learners can explore how information is divided into usable sections, converted into embeddings, retrieved based on relevance, and provided to a language model as context. The published upGrad curriculum includes RAG pipelines, embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, context-aware question answering, chunking, retrieval strategies, and troubleshooting hallucinations. Exploring Agentic AI Workflows Agentic AI introduces another layer of functionality. Instead of limiting an AI application to a single response, an agentic workflow can involve multiple steps, tools, decisions, and actions. A simplified workflow could look like: Goal → Planning → Tool Selection → Action → Evaluation → Next Step → Final Output For example, an AI agent designed for business research could potentially identify a task, retrieve relevant information, process the information, and prepare a structured result.A Generative AI and Agentic AI Course in Indore can provide a structured environment for developing these skills through guided learning, technical exercises, and project-based application. Learning these concepts gives students an opportunity to understand how AI systems can move from simple question-answering toward multi-step workflows. The AI Pro curriculum includes multi-step agent workflows, tool calling, autonomous task execution, API integration, reasoning and decision flows, memory-based planning, and failure-handling concepts. Learning Through Hands-On Projects Practical projects can help transform technical concepts into usable skills. The published program information states that learners work on 15+ live projects, with examples covering RAG systems, AI agents, and deployed GenAI applications. Potential project areas include: 1. Enterprise Document Intelligence Learners can explore an AI system capable of searching, summarising, and answering questions from a collection of documents. 2. Autonomous Workflow Agent A project can demonstrate how an agent plans tasks, interacts with tools, and performs multiple operations. 3. title: Beyond the Beep: Transitioning from Legacy IVR to LLM-Powered Conversational Voice Agents for Scalable Customer Service
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

keywords: interactive voice response; large language models; customer service automation; speech-to-text; intention understanding; multilingual support; micro, small and medium enterprises; call centers
topics: AI in Service Interactions; Speech and dialogue systems; Artificial Intelligence Applications
abstract: Traditional Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems, characterized by rigid "press 1 for service" menus, have long been a source of customer friction and operational bottleneck. This paper explores the fundamental paradigm shift toward LLM-powered conversational agents that utilize advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and real-time Speech-to-Text (STT) to provide human-like phone interactions. By leveraging Large Language Models, these agents can understand complex intent, maintain context, and resolve queries without the frustrating loops of legacy technology. The study examines the technological architecture required for a low-latency "neural loop" and analyses its impact on key business metrics such as Average Handle Time (AHT) and First Call Resolution (FCR). Furthermore, the research highlights successful implementations within the Indian context, specifically focusing on multilingual support for the MSME sector. The study concludes that the integration of conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI) is essential for businesses seeking to provide 24/7, high-quality support without the linear costs associated with traditional human-centric call centers.

title: Beyond Static Aids: A Contextual AR Framework for Prospective Memory Retrieval
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Milton Lucas Kakupa; Venkatramana Bhat P
